findings.title: Completed plugin-request logs no longer include the trace ID
findings.body: The previous implementation explicitly extracted `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` and appended it as `traceID` to every `Plugin Request Completed` entry. That extraction was removed. The new contextual middleware only installs endpoint, plugin, datasource, and user attributes, so materializing the logger with `FromContext` does not supply the removed trace field. This breaks correlation between backend plugin request logs and distributed traces; retain the explicit trace attribute or add it when building the contextual attributes, and cover it with a logging test.

findings.title: Adding a required method to the exported Logger interface is source-incompatible
findings.body: `Logger` is an exported interface, and adding `FromContext` means every existing implementation, wrapper, fake, or downstream mock of `pkg/plugins/log.Logger` will no longer compile until it implements the new method. This is a breaking API change beyond the middleware rename. Preserve compatibility by keeping `Logger` unchanged and introducing a separate optional contextual-logger interface that callers can type-assert, or explicitly version/document this breaking contract change.

findings.title: TestLogger drops log observations when LoggerMiddleware calls FromContext
findings.body: `LoggerMiddleware` now always logs through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)`, but this fake returns a newly allocated, unreferenced `TestLogger`. Tests that inject a `TestLogger` and inspect the original instance will observe zero log calls, and cannot verify the completed-request log or its attributes. Make `FromContext` return the same fake or a contextual clone sharing the same recorded log storage, then add coverage for the migrated contextual logging behavior.
